messages:
alex: FYI I'm opening a refresh PR for the quickstart sequence: aim to make the Hello World app literally 5 lines + a tiny local Docker section, consolidate auth examples across Node/Python/Go to the new SDK init, and add a short migration note for old env names. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/459. Can docs/devex triage?
maria: awesome. Can we also standardize on RW_API_KEY in examples (we still have RED_SESSION_KEY in a couple spots)? I can run a quick grep and replace.
lee: I'll audit the Go snippet. We used a custom client init there that doesn't match the latest SDK constructor. I'll push a replacement.
anya: Suggestion: for local testing keep a curl example first so folks who don't install SDKs can try quickly. Then show SDK examples. Short curl example should mention region host selection (api.redwood.ai vs api.redwood.eu).
alex: yes to curl-first. Proposed curl:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"open-redwood/1.0","input":"Hello from curl"}'
```
maria: tiny nit: include an example of setting RW_API_KEY in mac/linux bash: export RW_API_KEY=... and show Console path: Console -> Settings -> API Tokens.
lee: Go snippet fix pushed. New constructor: client := redwood.New(redwood.Config{APIKey: os.Getenv("RW_API_KEY")}) and Generate(ctx, opts). Works with our quickstart.
anya: For the Docker section can we keep it minimal: FROM node:18, copy, npm install, CMD node index.js. Then show how to build and run with RW_API_KEY env var.
alex: yes. I'll add a 3-line Dockerfile and run example: docker build -t rw-hello . && docker run -e RW_API_KEY=$RW_API_KEY rw-hello
maria: also saw a broken internal link to /docs/auth/setup that 404s after the nav rename. I'll file a redirect and update the link in the PR.
lee: one more thing: we should add a migration table that maps legacy env names -> current ones (RED_SERVER_KEY -> RW_API_KEY, OLD_RED_HOST -> RW_API_HOST). I'll draft it in the PR.
anya: CI idea: add a lightweight GH Action job that validates code snippets run without syntax errors (use node --check, python -m py_compile, go vet). Mark it opt-in via a secret so it doesn't run in forks.
alex: that's great. Add a test step that runs snippet lints only. No real network calls.
deploy-bot: Preview available for PR #459: https://deploy.preview.redwood.ai/pr-459 (expires in 7 days).
maria: thanks deploy-bot. I'll do a docs spellcheck and then review the Go + Node diffs. If everything looks good and CI is green, we can merge by EOD.
lee: left comments on the Go section about error handling and added a one-liner to mention timeout contexts.
anya: updated the curl example to show EU host alternative and added a footnote about region-aware endpoints.
alex: perfect. I'm going to squash minor fixes and merge once CI passes. Will add a blurb to the onboarding changelog mentioning the auth env rename and Docker quickstart.
maria: thumbs up. After merge I'll send a short thread in #onboarding to flag the migration note for any internal users.
